messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on freeways, 35 mph on expressways, 25 mph on city streets.
• “No speed limit” zones exist in some rural areas; drivers must drive at a safe speed. | | **Seat‑belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Violations carry a $50 fine and points on the driver’s record. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol‑abuse treatment, and possible jail time. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Failure to stop can lead to a $200 fine. | | **Parking** | • Parking on sidewalks, crosswalks, or in front of fire hydrants is prohibited.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | | **Towing** | • Towing a vehicle requires a valid towing permit.
• Unauthorized towing can result in a $200 fine. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection. | | **Points System** | • Traffic violations accrue points.
• 12 points within 2 years can lead to license suspension. | | **Special Provisions** | • Texas has specific rules for “no‑stop” zones, “no‑passing” zones, and “no‑turn” zones.
• Certain counties may have additional local ordinances. | **Where to Find Official Texts** 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary source for all traffic laws. 2. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – Provides guidelines, forms, and updates. 3. **Texas Legislature Online** – For the most recent legislative changes. **Quick Tips** - Always check for local ordinances; some cities have stricter rules. - Keep your driver's handbook handy; it contains detailed explanations and examples. - If you’re unsure about a specific law, consult the TxDMV website or contact your local county court clerk.
